items.notes: Excerpt states outbox records publication intent in the same transaction and a relay may send it more than once; directly addresses relay behavior after commit.
Explains that favorable latency can coexist with failed freshness and does not prove a universal claim, but gives no stopping criterion.
Quorum arithmetic and failure tolerance only; does not discuss shard write capacity or why added replicas fail to increase it.
Defines recall@k against independently judged relevant items, but does not address what happens when that judged set is incomplete.
Describes timeout-dominated overload with 0.05% rejection, not overload while rejecting most requests; different regime.
Experiment overview says the stage schedule is varied, but gives no declared traffic-share values.
States a pre-commit log is not evidence of accepted state and requires an authoritative reservation identity; directly separates business success from emission.
Table notes authentication and isolation controls do not prove object-level authorization, but does not address a tenant identifier specifically.
Cites bounded variable-length traversal and explosion/pruning concerns as source coverage, but provides no method for bounding a query.
Discusses eligible events, good outcomes and observation windows and links to SLI/objective material, but does not distinguish indicator from objective.
Says average requests per second conceal burst and hot-key pressure; no discussion of uniform-key test design.
States means cannot predict p99 and warns about measurement boundaries, but does not explain why p99 cannot substitute for mean residence time in Little's Law.
Contrasts trace correlation with durable, immutable per-operation audit identity and retention; directly explains why a trace ID is not a substitute.
States unstable tie-breaking: events at the same time depend on hash order; directly answers how equal-time ties are resolved.
Volume scope statement about evidence and limits; does not discuss replication counts or uncertainty about the input distribution.
Lists a common workload, seeds and per-1000-successful-request cost, which support comparability, but does not state the comparability principle.
Explains provenance binding inputs, engine run and output record, but does not state what happens to a derived record when canonical inputs change.
